ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (Act No. 16621, effective Dec. 31, 2019, as amended) and its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 31772, May 12, 2021); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Proceeds of Crimes (Act No. 15982, effective Dec. 18, 2018); Commercial Act (Act No. 16108, effective Jan. 16, 2019), Articles 289, 291, 292, 296 and 317; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 18065, effective Apr. 20, 2021) for foreign investors; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Act No. 15516, effective Apr. 17, 2018). Beneficial ownership identification obligations are governed by Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) rules and the Financial Transaction Reports Act, requiring customer due diligence for corporate entities with a minimum 25% ownership threshold.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Copy of Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office of the Republic of Korea (District Court Commercial Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path (receiver is an Apostille Convention state): issue certified court registry extract, where required have the extract first notarized, then apply to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) for an Apostille certificate. Consular Legalization path (receiver is not an Apostille Convention state): issue certified court registry extract, apply to MOFA for legalization, then submit to the destination-state consulate for final consular authentication. The two paths are parallel, mutually exclusive, and never chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Tax Compliance Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (individual district tax office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain NTS tax compliance certificate, notarize the officer's signature if required, then submit to MOFA for Apostille. Consular Legalization path: obtain NTS certificate, authenticate at MOFA, then process at the destination consulate. Only one path may be used; do not combine Apostille and consular procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney (PoA) for Incorporation and Banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa and a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: signed board resolution or PoA is notarized before a Korean notary, then MOFA affixes an Apostille; no consular authentication is required for Apostille member jurisdictions. Consular Legalization path: notarized resolution or PoA is legalized by MOFA and then by the destination-state consulate. These are alternative pathways, never consecutive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public who authenticates the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarized Articles of Association are submitted to MOFA for Apostille; the receiving foreign authority accepts the Apostille without further consular action. Consular Legalization path: notarized Articles are processed through MOFA legalization and then the destination consulate. The legalization route is determined solely by the destination country's membership in the Hague Apostille Convention and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from a Korean Commercial Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean licensed commercial bank maintaining the Chusik Hoesa's provisional or post-incorporation corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: bank letter is issued on bank letterhead, bank officer's signature is notarized, then MOFA issues an Apostille for Apostille Convention recipients. Consular Legalization path: notarized bank letter is authenticated by MOFA and then by the destination-state embassy/consulate. The chosen authentication route is exclusive to the receiving jurisdiction and must not be duplicated.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership and UBO Declaration Certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public and the Founding Shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarized UBO declaration with supporting identity and ownership documents is submitted to MOFA for Apostille for Apostille Convention states. Consular Legalization path: notarized declaration is legalized at MOFA and then at the destination-state consulate for non-member states. The two routes are mutually exclusive and must never be used in sequence on the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), and authorized signatories must be screened at intake, then continuously at least every 90 days, against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List and non-SDN sanctions lists; (iii) the European Union and United Kingdom consolidated financial sanctions lists; (iv) the Republic of Korea's consolidated sanctions list maintained under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and relevant Security Council resolutions; and (v) FATF high-risk and non-cooperative jurisdictions. PEP status requires a written self-declaration, electronic commercial database search, and adverse-media screening in both Korean and English. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Any positive or ambiguous match must be escalated to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and, if appropriate, a suspicious transaction report must be filed under the Financial Transaction Reports Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registry Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea, with the official Korean Corporate Registry (Hanguk Beobin Deunggi) maintained by local district court commercial registry divisions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name of a Chusik Hoesa must be recorded in Hangul and must contain the legal-form marker equivalent to Stock Corporation. English, Chinese, or other foreign-language transliterations may be used only as a secondary or trade-use name after the Hangul governing name has been cleared and registered; the Hangul name remains controlling for statutory and registry purposes. The registry applies a de facto four-tier review when processing a corporate name: (1) legal-form suffix and structure, (2) textual uniqueness against existing registered trademarks and trade names, (3) prohibited or sensitive token screening, and (4) Hangul orthography and commonly recognized representation standards to avoid consumer confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a proposed corporate name, the applicant may file an objection through the same Internet Registry Office within 14 days of receiving the rejection notice. The objection must state the legal basis for admissibility, the proposed Hangul name, and why the rejected name is not identical or deceptively similar to existing names and does not contain prohibited tokens. The supervising register judge will review the objection administratively, and the applicant may request a documentary re-examination. If the register judge rejects the objection a second time, the applicant may apply for a judicial appeal to the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act within 14 days; during the appeal the applicant should submit a revised name candidate to avoid further delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not categorically prohibited at the registry stage for a low-risk engineering CAD and BIM outsourcing company, provided the virtual office provider has a physical street address within the jurisdictional territory of the registered court and the applicant executes a valid serviced-office rental agreement. However, the National Tax Service (NTS) generally disallows a pure mail-forwarding address for corporate domicile, VAT invoicing, and employment tax purposes, and Korean commercial banks will ordinarily conduct a physical due-diligence visit before opening a corporate operating account. A serviced office with a dedicated meeting room and reception desk is recommended over a mailbox-only arrangement. For the ISIC 7110 business scope, Korean banks and tax authorities will expect the registered office to reflect genuine administrative substance, including books and records, business correspondence, and employee supervision, even if the actual CAD drafting occurs offshore.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low-to-moderate, approximately 15% during the first tax year, for a low-risk, standard-tier offshore engineering services entity. The risk increases if tax registration data, lease contracts, utility payments, or business filings show inconsistencies. Checklist: (1) valid lease agreement or office-use certificate; (2) on-site signboard or tenant plaque showing the registered business name; (3) visible workspace, computers, and files; (4) electricity, internet, and communication records in the company name; (5) VAT invoices and corporate accounting records at the registered office; (6) employment contract and payroll records for any local staff; and (7) corporate bank statements confirming operational activity. An unannounced physical inspection by NTS field officers or municipal tax officers may occur without prior notice, and failure to locate the registered office or any business records may result in administrative sanctions and involuntary closure proceedings.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 10000, as amended), particularly Articles 288 through 317 on incorporation of stock corporations, including Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 295 (payment of subscription price), Article 302 (incorporation meeting), Article 306 (appointment of representatives), and Article 317 (registration of incorporation); also relevant Articles 361, 393, and 412 on board powers and duties.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; for Seoul, the Registration Office of the Seoul Central District Court, also accessible online through the Korean Court Internet Registration Service at www.iros.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa Company Registration Application) submitted under Article 317 of the Commercial Act and the applicable Supreme Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. Each issued share must have a par value of at least KRW 100, and the total paid-in capital is fixed in the Articles of Incorporation. Subscription proceeds must be fully paid before registration and placed into a designated bank subscription deposit account that is restricted or blocked until the registration certificate is issued. There is no central government escrow account; the bank certificate of subscription payment is submitted to the Registry as proof of capital payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION)

RESOLVED, that the First Board of Directors of the Corporation, duly convened at the registered office in the Republic of Korea with the requisite quorum of directors present throughout, acting in accordance with the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation, does hereby adopt the following resolutions:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE OF SHARES. The Board certifies that the initial share capital of the Corporation is established as set out in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into [number] Ordinary Shares with a par value of KRW [100] per share. All issued shares have been lawfully subscribed and fully paid in cash by the incorporators as evidenced by the Share Subscription Schedule and the Bank Deposit Certificate issued by [bank name]. The Board accepts such subscription and payment, confirms the aggregate paid-in capital amount of KRW [amount], and directs that such amount be recorded in the Corporation's share capital account. The Board further authorizes the issuance of physical share certificates against surrender of the subscription receipt.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts as the registered office of the Corporation the address [full address], Republic of Korea, within the territorial jurisdiction of the [District Court Registration Office]. The Representative Director is authorized to execute, deliver, and maintain any lease, sublease, landlord consent, and utility authorization necessary to preserve the registered office and to give public notice of any change if required by law.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the Representative Director, together with any designated director or officer, to open, operate, and maintain all corporate bank accounts, including domestic currency accounts, foreign-currency accounts, wire-transfer receiving accounts, and online payment settlement facilities. The Representative Director is specifically authorized to execute account opening forms, signature cards, wire transfer instructions, banking mandates, and electronic banking agreements, including payment rails consistent with the Corporation's invoicing to offshore BIM and structural drafting clients. Any two authorized signatories shall execute instruments above an internal control threshold established by the Board.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board ratifies and confirms the appointment of the initial statutory officers as previously elected by the incorporators, namely [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Director, and [Name] as Statutory Auditor if required by law or the Articles of Incorporation. Each appointee has accepted office in writing, and the Board confirms their respective terms of service, powers, delegated authorities, and remuneration.

5. CORPORATE FORMALITIES. The Board authorizes the Representative Director to affix the corporate seal, obtain authenticated registry certificates, file the business registration with the National Tax Service, register the Corporation for mandatory payroll and social insurance accounts, and issue any share certificates or corporate instruments incident to the commencement of offshore Building Information Modeling, structural drafting, and engineering CAD outsourcing operations.

Adopted by unanimous resolution of all directors present at this meeting and entered into the minute book on the date first written above.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize Articles of Incorporation and block paid-in share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed under the Korean Notary Public Act, in coordination with a licensed commercial bank in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, setting out the corporate name, corporate purpose, total authorized share capital, total shares issued at incorporation, par value of at least KRW 100 per share, registered office address, public notice method, and initial officers. The incorporators must execute every page of the final instrument, after which a Korean-licensed notary public must notarize the Articles. In parallel, open a subscription deposit account at a licensed Korean commercial bank and deposit the full aggregate subscription price into that account so that the funds are blocked or restricted until company registration. Obtain a bank certificate evidencing full payment and the restricted status of funds. This step satisfies the payment condition under Article 295 of the Commercial Act before the Registration application is submitted.
required_dossiers: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription schedule and payment ledger
Bank subscription deposit certificate showing full blocked payment
Copies of incorporators' passports or identity cards
Power of attorney for any representative subscriber
Articles of Incorporation translation if required by the Registry
Corporate seal registration application and seal impression card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary objects to a defect in the draft or the bank certificate is insufficient, correct the instrument, re-execute the conformed pages, and obtain a renewed bank certificate. If the Registry later queries the authenticity of payment, submit a notarized confirmation from the bank and the incorporators.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene incorporators meeting and appoint first directors and statutory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators of the Chusik Hoesa meeting pursuant to Articles 299 through 306 of the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before registration, convene an incorporators meeting or obtain unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting. The incorporators must affirm that all issued shares have been subscribed and paid, elect the first directors and statutory auditor if any, fix the term of office, approve the compensation of directors, adopt the registered office address, and authorize the execution of the incorporation registration. The chairperson must sign the minutes, and each appointed director and auditor must execute a written acceptance of office. If unanimous written consent is used in place of a physical meeting, the document must be signed by all incorporators and state all statutory matters required by the Commercial Act. This document forms the governance basis for the first board resolutions after registration.
required_dossiers: Minutes of incorporators meeting or unanimous written consent
Written acceptance of office from each director and auditor
Directors' and auditor's identification documents
Approved share subscription and payment report
Stated capital allocation schedule
Confirmation of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the meeting is challenged for improper notice or procedural defects, reconvene a corrective incorporators meeting or obtain a unanimous ratification consent. If a director acceptance is missing, obtain a backdated written acceptance signed after the meeting and attach an explanatory statement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration with the District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, electrically through www.iros.go.kr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation together with all statutory annexes to the competent District Court Registration Office, either in person or online through the Korean Court Internet Registration Service. Pay the registration tax based on paid-in capital, the local education tax on such registration tax, and the court filing fee, and attach proof of payment. The application must be signed by the incorporators or their authorized agent and must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank certificate of paid-in subscription, incorporators meeting minutes or written consent, written acceptances of directors and auditor, and lease or landlord consent confirming the registered office. The court examiner will review legal compliance, issue corrections if necessary, and upon final approval enter the corporation into the commercial registry and issue the certificate of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Company Registration application form signed by incorporators
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of incorporators meeting or unanimous written consent
Bank certificate of full paid-in subscription amount
Written acceptances of the directors and statutory auditor
Lease agreement or landlord consent for registered office
Power of attorney if filing through an agent or attorney
Proof of payment of registration tax, education tax, and court fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query, correction order, or suspension notice, respond within the statutory correction period by filing the requested supplementary materials, paying any additional tax or stamp fee, and obtaining a written statement from the examiner. If the application was filed in the wrong district court, apply for transfer to the court with correct territorial jurisdiction and refile the dossiers without losing the original filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activate corporate banking, business tax registration, and seal certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office; local municipal authorities; and licensed commercial banks in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation and authenticated copy of the commercial register, apply to the National Tax Service for issuance of the Business Registration Certificate under the Value-Added Tax Act. Register the corporate seal impression with the relevant municipal authority and obtain a corporate seal certificate. Use the authenticated registry certificate, corporate seal certificate, Business Registration Certificate, and the First Board Resolution banking authorization to open the operating bank account and to establish wire and online settlement facilities for receiving payments from offshore BIM and CAD clients. If employees will be hired, register the corporation with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Workers' Compensation Insurance systems within the statutory deadlines.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation
Authenticated copy of commercial registry
Corporate seal certificate
Business Registration Certificate application documents
First Board Resolution on banking authorization
Director identification and corporate seal
Registered office lease and utility proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office challenges the business purpose or requests clarification, submit an engineering service contract or outsourcing agreement evidencing offshore CAD/BIM services. If the bank compliance department imposes additional due diligence, provide organizational documents, registry certificates, and a board-approved customer due diligence file. If registration is delayed, request an expedited tax office review through the National Tax Service guidance window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue share certificates and complete post-incorporation statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, supported by the corporate secretary and external counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first formal board meeting after registration to ratify all pre-incorporation contracts, adopt the share register, approve the issuance of share certificates, fix the corporate seal usage rules, and approve the banking signatory mandate. Issue share certificates under the corporate seal and enter all subscribers in the shareholders register. The board must also approve the accounting year, initial accounting policies, and the statutory auditor's engagement if applicable. Maintain a corporate minute book, share certificate ledger, director and auditor registers, and statutory records at the registered office. This step ensures that the corporate governance package is complete for subsequent tax registrations, client contracts, and bank compliance requirements.
required_dossiers: First Board meeting minutes
Share register and share certificate stubs
Corporate seal and seal register
Shareholder list and subscriber identification files
Directors and auditor appointment register
Board-approved accounting policies and fiscal year election
Registered office statutory records book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share certificate is defective or lost before delivery, the board shall approve cancellation, issue a substitute certificate after receiving a bond of indemnity, and record the replacement in the share certificate ledger. If the minutes omit a required item, adopt a supplemental board resolution ratifying the omission and attach it to the original minute book.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is engaged in pure offshore digital engineering, CAD drafting, and Building Information Modeling consulting services under ISIC 7110 and NAICS 541330, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility in Korea.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is triggered by CAD/BIM consultancy and structural drafting activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no EIA, Environmental Registration, or Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required because the business will not construct or operate any physical industrial source, plant, or facility in Korea.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the entity generates no wastewater, VOC emissions, hazardous waste, fixed-source pollutants, or environmental discharges. Any leased office space must comply with ordinary building utility rules administered by the landlord and local government.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no civil defense fire safety permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval is required for pure office-based digital engineering services. The landlord must maintain the building's fire evacuation certificates and structural safety obligations, and the entity must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act if it hires employees in Korea, including mandatory accident insurance registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating through the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal at hometax.go.kr; customs and export clearance matters are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS single-window portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident foreign entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa or directly undertaking taxable business activities in South Korea, the entity or its statutory tax representative must first obtain a business registration certificate (Business Registration Number) from the competent district tax office or via the NTS Home Tax Service web portal. The application must be filed using the official business registration application form together with the foreign entity's certificate of incorporation, certificates of representative appointment, the tax representative's power of attorney, proof of local place of business (or representative designation agreement), and any organizational documents requested by the NTS. The NTS will issue a ten-digit or twelve-digit registration number which simultaneously functions as the VAT identification number for indirect tax purposes. The tax representative becomes jointly responsible for filing, keeping records, and cooperating with NTS audits during the period of representation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value Added Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold. Any entrepreneur, including a Chusik Hoesa engaged in taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea, is under a legal duty to register for VAT through the NTS. A simplified VAT regime exists for certain small-scale individual entrepreneurs with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but this does not constitute a registration exemption and does not apply to ordinary corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices under the NTS Home Tax Service are mandatory for B2B taxable supplies; the electronic tax invoice must contain the standardized invoice ID, digital signature of the issuer, and must be transmitted via NTS-approved EDI/API channels by the last day of the month in which the supply is made. The NTS maintains a centralized digital validation and receipt system for real-time matching between issuers and recipients; cash receipts are also mandatory for certain consumer B2C sales. Businesses meeting statutory turnover thresholds must issue all tax invoices electronically; any manual paper invoices remain allowed only in narrowly prescribed exceptional cases.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, zero-rating at 0% applies to exported goods where the goods leave Korea under an export customs declaration, and to qualifying services rendered to non-residents, performed wholly or partly in Korea and supplied for the purpose of facilitating export or providing offshore engineering services such as CAD/BIM structural drafting for non-resident clients. The taxpayer must retain documentary evidence proving the export nature of the transaction, the offshore status of the recipient, delivery or performance abroad, and settlement in foreign currency through a legitimate foreign exchange transaction. Zero-rating is a statutory entitlement once the legal conditions are satisfied; no prior NTS approval is required but substantiation on audit is mandatory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Bill of Entry / Shipping Bill) lodged with the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing shipment from Korea
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate / Foreign Exchange Remittance Confirmation demonstrating inward receipt of export proceeds
Service Contract or Purchase Order clearly identifying the non-resident recipient and the offshore nature of the CAD/BIM drafting services
Other bank or SWIFT records proving foreign currency remittance from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating is claimed without supporting export declarations, without valid foreign exchange settlement, or where export proceeds are not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period (unless a lawful extension is obtained from the relevant authorities), the NTS will reverse the zero-rated treatment and assess output VAT at 10%, together with statutory surcharges and interest. Cases of fraud, false invoicing, or wilful non-substantiation may attract penalties up to 40% of the under-declared tax and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. Customs and foreign exchange authorities may additionally impose sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Customs Act for non-repatriation of export proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); Korea Customs Service supervises export settlement mechanics and the Foreign Exchange Information System supported by BOK for transaction reporting
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly liberalized current-account and capital-account regime under FETA, but Korean won (KRW) is not a globally freely convertible currency outside the onshore banking network. Capital-account transactions require mandatory reporting to a designated Foreign Exchange Bank and, where FETA thresholds are exceeded, prior or ex-post filing with MOEF. Dividends and profits can be remitted abroad only after corporate tax obligations are settled and after the Korean bank verifies the supporting board resolution, audited financial statements, and the standard Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code for profit remittance. Current-account service exports, including engineering and drafting services, are not subject to prior approval, but all receipts and payments must flow through a Korean foreign exchange bank using proper underlying contract documentation. Surrender rules are lenient: export proceeds must be collected within one year from the export declaration date and must be brought into a domestic foreign-currency account or converted at a bank at the prevailing market rate, but there is no mandatory statutory conversion percentage. The KRW market remains protected by position limits and genuine-exposure requirements for hedging; speculative non-underlying derivative activity is tightly restricted. Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) transactions are permitted only through authorized domestic financial institutions and subject to Financial Supervisory Service position limits, not as a free offshore KRW hedging vehicle. Overall, the system is administratively open but documentary intense: a compliant Korean Chusik Hoesa must maintain real contracts, authentic invoices, and accurate Foreign Exchange Information System codes for every cross-border flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected and delivered to a Korean foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of export declaration; an extension may be granted by the Minister of Economy and Finance or the designated bank under FETA. No fixed percentage of KRW surrender is imposed on industrial outsourcing receipts; the full foreign-currency amount may be credited to a Foreign Currency Demand Deposit Account at a Tier-1 Korean bank. Any conversion of such foreign exchange into KRW must occur through a domestic foreign exchange bank at market rates and must be supported by the underlying service agreement and standard collection document template.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability rating: Low as a primary treasury rail, and Medium only as a supplementary cross-border collection channel. Offshore fintech EMIs, including Wise, are not licensed Korean banks and cannot legally open an onshore KRW demand deposit account or provide a domestic Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute (KFTC) clearing number. Under South Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act, only licensed electronic financial institutions and banks under FSS registration may provide payment or fund-transfer services in KRW. Wise therefore acts as a money-transfer intermediary routing through a licensed partner bank and cannot serve as the statutory account held by the Korean Chusik Hoesa for capital contribution, payroll, tax payments, or trade settlement. The entity should maintain all statutory flows through Tier-1 Korean bank accounts; Wise may be used for small collection of overseas milestone fees only if the Korean bank is fully informed and the underlying FX reporting is completed.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: An in-branch physical appearance is the default expectation for a statutory director or legalized attorney-in-fact opening a Korean corporate account. The Real Name Financial Transaction Act and FIU guidance require strong identification and face-to-face verification for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not universally recognized; most Korean banks accept an apostilled power-of-attorney only when accompanied by notarized passport identification and a video call with the bank's compliance officer. The statutory director or a named attorney-in-fact should plan to appear physically at a branch in Seoul or Busan. Fully remote electronic onboarding for an externally managed foreign-owned engineering company is rarely approved by tier-1 banks due to CDD mandates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with no Korean credit or tax history controlling a newly formed Chusik Hoesa without mandatory minimum capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and apostilled certificate of incorporation and registered director list; passport or national ID copies of the UBO and all directors; a signed KYCC/AML questionnaire and latest comprehensive tax return from the UBO's resident jurisdiction; a corporate biographical statement for a persona/engineering company; three years of overseas business records; and a detailed source-of-funds narrative covering the initial equity contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial equity injection arriving from an offshore individual remitter rather than from the identified institutional group company, creating a potential layering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a board resolution of the Korean Chusik Hoesa authorizing share issuance; foreign direct investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) submitted to the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the designated FX bank; bank statement from the remitter's overseas account; proof of employment salary or ownership dividend source; For Indian? Actually for Korea: notarized audited accounts of remitter, if corporate; tax documentation proving legitimate source of funds; and an escrow account deposit receipt from the Korean bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Correspondence mismatch between ISIC 7110 architectural/engineering directorship and payment recipient names because the entity is a CAD/BIM outsourcing vendor with no physical Korean office staff
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a detailed business plan with signed client contracts from Korea and overseas counterparts; BIM/structural service agreements with defined scope-of-work; export invoice schedules; taxable-business registration certificate from the Korean tax authorities; payroll and subcontracting records showing the company's operational footprint; and a legalized office lease either virtual or physical asset service agreement proving a genuine Korean presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment rails include Wise and frequent small-amount wire transfers without a matching trade TLEC trade ledger? Use trade log; red flag for unexplained service revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain an actively updated trade ledger showing each Wise or wire transfer matched to a specific contract milestone; include the customer PO, accepted BIM/CAD deliverable report, QR-code versioning record, and project-specific invoice; provide the bank with a quarterly reconciliation pack and FETA purpose-code mapping; obtain an undertaking that no proceeds from gaming, forex trading, cryptocurrency, or prohibited industries flow into the account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial capital injection must be wired under SWIFT MT103 through a designated Korean Foreign Exchange Bank. The originating remitter must identify the Korean Chusik Hoesa by corporate name, domestic account IBAN-equivalent designation, and bank address. The bank will classify the remittance under the Foreign Exchange Information System code for non-resident foreign direct investment or stock acquisition, attaching the share subscription resolution and corporate identity documents. The entity must file a Foreign Investment Report under FIPA before the funds can be credited as statutory capital; after receipt the bank will issue a foreign investment registration certificate and the funds are held in a Capital Escrow Account, later converted into the Basic Operational Currency Account. If no foreign investment report is required, the funds must be reported under FETA as inbound overseas remittance for corporate funding and will be subject to standard source-of-funds evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local operating costs, payroll, and Korean taxes are cleared through domestic KFTC-based corporate current accounts using Korean electronic settlement rails. Cross-border trade disbursements must be routed as SWIFT MT103 from the US dollar or KRW foreign-currency account with a fully stated Korean FX purpose code. For engineering services, outgoing payments should use standard service-import clearing via telegraphic transfer; commercial letters of credit are acceptable only if clients require formal documentary instruments, but will be structured against acceptance certificates and CAD/BIM transfer protocols. Documentary collections are viable for recurring milestone deliverables only where a transport document is not applicable; in practice Korea accepts MT103 service payment documentation consisting of signed monthly valuation certificates and tax invoices. All outbound FX payments must be supported by the bank's internal Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW forward contracts with a designated Korean foreign exchange bank, up to twelve months tenor, supported by signed export service contracts and an underlying exposure declaration under FETA

Korean won / offsetting currency swaps used strictly to hedge the cash-flow mismatch between USD-denominated BIM receivables and KRW-denominated payroll and local operating expenses; such swaps must be covered by the same trade ledger and cannot be detached from the underlying operational exposure

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only through an authorized domestic financial institution within Financial Supervisory Service position limits, and only as a temporary hedge for non-KRW or non-kibol accounted; NDFs must not be used as speculative return generators because of the genuine-exposure rule and monthly position ceiling

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and tax reconciliation statement for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; extended to May 31 where the return is prepared and accompanied by tax adjustment statements signed by a licensed tax accountant or certified public accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or unfaithful filing incurs a penalty of 20% of the underreported amount or 40% for omission or improper refund claims, plus statutory delinquency interest of 3.4% per annum on unpaid tax; prolonged non-filing permits the NTS to assess the tax ex officio, revoke the business registration, and impose a local-tax collection order, but does not automatically strike off the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return (provincial/city portion) under the Local Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Si/Gun/Gu) of the registered head office via the WETAX portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end where the national corporate tax return is filed by March 31; if the national return is validly extended to May 31, the local return is due by June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted local income tax returns add a careless-declaration penalty of up to 40% of understated tax and a local delinquency charge at the statutory rate; continued non-compliance exposes assets to local-tax compulsory collection and enforcement, yet it does not by itself dissolve the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of shareholders for approval of annual financial statements, dividends, and appointment or reappointment of statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act; the approved minutes are kept in the corporate minute book and no registry filing is required unless officers or articles are changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting subjects directors to an administrative fine not exceeding KRW 5,000,000 under the Commercial Act and creates evidence of no business substance for the tax authorities; persistent inaction can lead to closure of the business registration and may invite court inspection or shareholder injunctions, but ordinary strike-off is not a summary remedy in Korea.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited annual financial statements (only if the company is an audit-subject Chusik Hoesa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART filing system for securities-reporting companies; a copy is also made available to shareholders and attached to the tax return where relevant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For securities-reporting companies, within 14 days after the audit report is delivered to the company and before the annual general meeting; for non-listed audit-target companies, in time to be laid before the shareholders at the annual meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted submission of the statutory audit report to the FSS triggers a penalty under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, possible designation of an auditor by the Financial Services Commission, and suspension of auditor report recognition; for tax purposes, absent audited accounts, the NTS may disregard the books and assess the 20/40% unfaithful-return penalty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax adjustment returns for the January-June and July-December taxable periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 for the first half and January 25 for the second half of the fiscal calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid or unfaithful VAT is subject to a 10% general negligence penalty, a 0.5% penalty on false tax invoice amounts, and statutory delinquency interest; repeated non-filing of VAT is a direct administrative factor used by the NTS to cancel the business registration and may result in criminal referral for tax-invoice violations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual report of a foreign-invested company (applicable only when the Chusik Hoesa is classified as a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or the delegated foreign-investment administrative agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual report or a 30-day change report may incur administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and loss of foreign-investment incentives; it does not by itself strike off the Korean entity but supports administrative compliance escalation by the foreign investment authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified public accountant audit is required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies when any of the following is present at the relevant fiscal year-end: (i) total assets are KRW 12 billion or more (approximately USD 9.1 million); (ii) the company is a securities-reporting issuer listed on KOSPI, KOSDAQ, or any other KRX market; (iii) the company is a financial institution, insurer, securities firm, asset management company, or other financial investment business entity under a special act; (iv) the company has total annual revenue of KRW 10 billion or more and an average workforce of 100 or more employees; or (v) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as a public-interest or otherwise audit-required company under the applicable Decree. No minimum capital threshold modifies this requirement, and exemption is not available on the ground that the business is a private offshore CAD/BIM outsourcing company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Companies subject to audit must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) if they are listed or public-interest entities; private companies may apply the general Korean GAAP applicable to unlisted corporations (SME accounting standards issued by the Korea Accounting Standards Board). Statutory audits are performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA) and the certified auditor is a member of the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24 percent national marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; the 10 percent local income tax surtax brings the combined top marginal rate to 26.4 percent.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea does not grant blanket corporate tax holidays. Preferential incentives are available under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act: R&D tax credits, job-creation credits, capital investment credits, SME reduced rates, and selective foreign-investment tax reductions in free economic zones. The national statutory tax brackets range from 9 percent to 24 percent before the local surtax, depending on taxable income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return and Self-Assessment Statement (Form 48 series), including the Tax Base and Amount Calculation Statement and supplementary schedules, submitted through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal (hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Domestic corporations: file within three months after the fiscal year-end. Foreign corporations with a Korean permanent establishment: file within four months after the fiscal year-end. An interim corporate tax return and prepayment is due within two months after the close of the first six-month period of a business year exceeding six months.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate business registration number (10-digit tax identification number).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the tax ID issued to the Korean branch or PE; do not enter the parent's foreign tax ID.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period (business year start and end dates).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the accounting period endorsed in the PE registration; changes require advance approval from the district tax office.
Include Korean-source revenue effectively connected with the PE, including fees from civil infrastructure CAD/BIM services and software licensing.
Allocate home-office general and administrative expenses using approved profit-attribution methodologies; maintain detailed documentation of intercompany service costs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income base after book-tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply transfer pricing adjustments, non-deductible expenditures, and withholding-type revenue adjustments; do not offset parent company NOLs against PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed before credits and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the progressive corporate income tax bands applicable to branches and add the 10 percent local income tax surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable after interim payments, credits, and special deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the balance in KRW by the statutory deadline and attach the reconciliation of treaty-withheld amounts if any.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized by an additional tax equal to 20 percent of the unpaid tax. False or omitted income triggers an additional tax of 20 percent, or 40 percent for concealment, plus delinquency charges of 0.025 percent per day. Criminal prosecution is available under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act for willful non-filing and evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22 percent aggregate statutory rate on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders (20 percent national tax plus 2 percent local surcharge), subject to reduction under applicable tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must deliver an original or certified copy of the tax residence certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction, complete a beneficial ownership declaration, and file the reduced-withholding application with the payer or the National Tax Service via HomeTax before payment. If the payer withholds at the statutory rate, the recipient may file a refund application through its Korean withholding agent within three years from the end of the statutory payment date.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate for cross-border interest and royalties is 22 percent aggregate (20 percent plus 2 percent local surcharge). Treaty rates normally reduce interest to 10 to 15 percent and royalties to 10 to 15 percent, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner, is not a conduit, and meets any limitation-on-benefits clause.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is mandatory when the annual value of cross-border intercompany transactions with foreign related parties exceeds KRW 5 billion. Master File documentation is required where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion and the Korean entity has cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion. A simplified foreign-related transaction disclosure is generally submitted when such transactions exceed KRW 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to Common Reporting Standard offshore hubs. Economic substance is tested through the general anti-avoidance rule, controlled foreign corporation rules, beneficial-ownership requirements in treaty cases, and the permanent establishment profit-attribution rule. A local vehicle that lacks employees, premises, business function, or decision-making authority in the CAD/BIM engineering outsourcing chain will be treated as a conduit, disregarded, and its profits reattributed to the economically active entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion / False Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-declaring Korean-source CAD/BIM revenue, inventing subcontract costs, issuing fabricated invoices, or concealing bank accounts and foreign wire receipts from the National Tax Service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax equal to 20 percent of the unpaid tax, rising to 40 percent for concealment or false invoices; daily delinquency charge of 0.025 percent; criminal liability of up to five years' imprisonment or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order or knowingly facilitate the evasion are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties, and collection costs; they can be subjected to asset seizure, travel bans, and imprisonment upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or maintaining a Chusik Hoesa with no physical office, no staff, no genuine business activity, and no local managerial function, used purely as an invoicing pass-through to strip profits from engineering intangibles or claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The shell will be disregarded under the substance-over-form doctrine; intercompany deductions will be disallowed, taxable income reconstructed on an arm's length basis, treaty withholding relief denied, and undistributed offshore income may be taxed under CFC rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced where the entity is a mere facade or instrument of fraud; directors face civil restitution and joint tax liability, plus court-imposed travel bans where collection is at risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving overseas engineering fees through personal or unregistered accounts, using layered wire transfers or Wise/BankWire pass-throughs to conceal the true beneficial owner, and failing to issue electronic tax invoices or report foreign exchange transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to issue electronic tax invoices attracts a surcharge of 2 percent of the supply value; violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act can result in administrative fines, seizure of undeclared funds, and criminal referral; banks may freeze the underlying accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or authorize such payment structures are personally liable for resulting penalties; they can be charged criminally, have assets confiscated, and be prohibited from leaving Korea pending investigation and enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare or submit Local File, Master File, or the foreign-related transaction disclosure within the NTS's statutory request period, or submitting inconsistent intercompany agreements or handwritten transaction records that cannot support the arm's length price for civil infrastructure BIM/CAD services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may recharacterize the transaction and adjust taxable income using its chosen transfer pricing method; a 20 percent additional tax applies to the understated tax, rising to 40 percent in cases of gross negligence or concealment, together with daily delinquency charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors responsible for filing and record retention may be named as joint assessment targets in willful non-compliance cases; repeated violations constitute an aggravating criminal factor and may trigger executive travel restrictions and prosecution.
